Shitrai
SHIT-rye
n. (the Sharonite, overseer of David's herds in Sharon)
Hebrew Shitray, my officers, or scribe-like, from shoter, an officer or overseer; named once, 1 Chronicles 27:29.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Shitrai held one of the twelve stewardships over David's property: “And over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite: and over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai” (1 Chronicles 27:29). The chapter is an inventory of administration. After the military courses and the tribal officers, the Chronicler lists the men set over the king's treasures, his fields, his vineyards, his olive and sycomore trees, his cellars of oil, his herds in Sharon and in the valleys, his camels, his asses and his flocks. Shitrai was the cattleman of the Sharon plain, the fertile coastal country where the best grazing in Israel lay, and he was a Sharonite — a local man set over the ground he came from. His name is built on the Hebrew word for an officer. Nothing else is said of him. The whole chapter is a quiet argument that David's reign was ordered down to the oil cellars, and the New Testament keeps the thought: he that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much, and a steward is required to be found faithful.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Shitrai, the Sharonite, overseer of David's herds that fed in Sharon, named once, 1 Chronicles 27:29.

Hebrew Shitray, my officers, from shoter, an officer or overseer.

Called the Sharonite, a man of the plain of Sharon.

It occurs once in the Authorized Version, 1 Chronicles 27:29.

He was set over the herds that fed in Sharon.

He is one of twelve stewards of David's property.

Key Scripture

1Ch 27:29 — "And over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite: and over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai:"

1Ch 27:31 — "And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagerite. All these were the rulers of the substance which was king David's."

1Ch 27:25 — "And over the king's treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel: and over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the castles, was Jehonathan the son of Uzziah:"

Luk 16:10 — "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much."

Modern Corruption

Material stewardship is held beneath spiritual concern; Scripture devotes a chapter to naming the men over David's cattle, oil and vineyards.

expand to see more

Two errors are corrected by 1 Chronicles 27. The first is the pietism that treats property, administration and accounts as beneath spiritual attention; the Holy Ghost saw fit to name the overseer of the king's sycomore trees. The second is the prosperity teaching that makes increase the proof of favour; the chapter is about management, not accumulation, and it closes by saying that all these were the rulers of the substance which was king David's — the substance belonged to the king, and the men were stewards of it.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that everything a man holds is held in trust. The Lord's parables of the talents, the pounds and the unjust steward all turn on it, and so does Paul's rule that it is required in stewards that a man be found faithful. Shitrai kept cattle in Sharon for a king, and his name is in the Bible because he kept them well.
